title: Ship team-based billing
desc: Per-seat subscriptions for teams, following docs/billing-plan.md. Target: live behind a feature flag by Friday.

summary: Plan registered: 11 tasks across Discovery, Build and Verify. Starting with the two discovery tasks in parallel.

text: Stripe is the payment provider. The plan references Stripe objects but never says it is mandated.
why: Billing plan section 2 uses Stripe terminology throughout

text: Legacy billing code lives in app/billing/legacy; 3 callers still import it.
Keep legacy invoices read-only instead of migrating them.
why: Migrating 40k rows has no stated requirement
alt: One-off backfill into the new schema

text: Mapped 14 files; 3 legacy callers need a compatibility shim
Webhook-driven state sync with idempotency keys, not polling.
Approach agreed; ADR written to docs/adr/012-billing-sync.md

summary: Discovery finished. Provider approach settled on webhook-driven sync; legacy code needs a thin shim. Moving into the build phase.
risks: Plan is silent on proration rules

text: Seat limits are enforced in the application layer, not by a database constraint.
why: Limits change per plan, so a constraint would need a migration each time
alt: Check constraint driven by a plans table

text: Should free-trial teams be capped at 5 seats?
The plan does not say how to prorate mid-cycle seat changes.
Reviewer asked for an index on subscriptions.team_id
Schema and migration merged, index added
Prorate seat changes to the day, matching Stripe default behaviour.
why: Plan is silent; this needs no custom logic
alt: Apply changes from the next billing cycle

text: Needs STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET for the test environment; not in the repo or CI secrets
Can you add a Stripe test-mode webhook secret to CI?
options: Use the Stripe CLI locally for now

text: Checkout session API with 9 passing tests
Seat picker caps at 50 seats, then shows "contact sales".
why: Common pattern; keeps large accounts on invoicing

summary: Checkout API is done and the seat UI is underway. Webhook handler (T4) is blocked on a CI secret, which holds up metering, tests and the security review. Two assumptions about proration and the provider need your eyes.
next: Unblock T4 (needs your answer on Q2)
risks: T7, T8, T9 and T11 are all waiting behind T4
Proration assumption (A4) is low confidence and high impact

text: Use the Stripe CLI locally for now; I will add the CI secret Monday
Using a locally generated secret from the Stripe CLI
Cap at 5 seats during trial
Stripe is correct
Apply seat changes from the next billing cycle instead
Seat UI shipped with cap and contact-sales state
Webhook handler with idempotency, retries and signature checks

Rewriting proration tests for next-cycle behaviour
Hourly metering job with backfill command
Migration guide and API docs updated
41 integration tests passing
Webhook endpoint verifies signatures and rejects replays older than 5 minutes.
No critical findings; one low-severity logging fix applied

summary: All 11 tasks are done. Team billing is complete behind the feature flag, with staged rollout planned. Remaining follow-up for you: add the Stripe test secret to CI.
